denomProfiles/church-of-scotland/tagline: The Kirk: Scotland's national Presbyterian church since the Reformation of 1560.
denomProfiles/church-of-scotland/coreDoc: The Westminster Confession is its principal subordinate standard, with liberty of opinion on points not essential.
The Articles Declaratory (1921) affirm its spiritual independence from the state.
Christ alone is King and Head of the Church.
Reformed teaching on grace, Scripture and the sacraments.
denomProfiles/church-of-scotland/focuses: Parish ministry to every community in Scotland.
Social care through CrossReach and community work.
Public life: the annual General Assembly debates national questions.
Ecumenism and the Iona Community's work for peace and justice.
denomProfiles/church-of-scotland/practic: Sermon-centred worship with psalms and hymns (Church Hymnary).
Kirk sessions, presbyteries and a General Assembly with an annual Moderator.
Communion celebrated a few times a year in many parishes, more often in others.
Women ordained as elders (1966) and ministers (1968).
Permitting ministers to conduct same-sex marriages since 2022.
denomProfiles/church-of-scotland/influen: Scottish missions and emigration spread Presbyterianism.
Formed at the Disruption of 1843 under Thomas Chalmers.
Scottish mission churches joined the 1970 union.
Shaped thinkers such as John McLeod Campbell and T. F. Torrance.
denomProfiles/church-of-scotland/inIndia: Its missions founded leading colleges: Alexander Duff's school in Calcutta (1830, now Scottish Church College), John Wilson's in Bombay and the Madras Christian College; Scottish missions in the Eastern Himalayas included Kalimpong.
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/tagline: The Netherlands' historic Reformed church and its 2004 Protestant union.
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/coreDoc: The Three Forms of Unity: Belgic Confession (1561), Heidelberg Catechism and Canons of Dort (1619).
The PKN also recognises the Augsburg Confession, Luther's Catechism and the Barmen Declaration.
Reformed teaching on grace and the sovereignty of God.
A wide spectrum from orthodox Reformed to liberal Protestant within one church.
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/focuses: Ministry in a highly secular society with rapidly declining membership.
Church–Israel relations, written into the PKN church order.
Diaconal and social work in local communities.
Managing diversity between the 'Bible belt' and liberal congregations.
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/practic: Sermon-centred worship with the Genevan psalms and the Liedboek (2013).
Infant baptism and Holy Supper, sometimes with the congregation seated at tables.
Presbyterial-synodal government by church councils, classes and a general synod.
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/influen: Founded in 1857 by Dutch Seceder immigrants in Michigan.
Reformed churches in South Africa and Indonesia
Planted through the Dutch East India Company and missions.
Kuyper and Bavinck influenced evangelical thought worldwide.
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/keyFigu: Leiden professor whose views Dort rejected
denomProfiles/dutch-reformed-pkn/inIndia: Dutch East India Company chaplains served Reformed congregations at Pulicat, Nagapattinam and Cochin in the 17th and 18th centuries; the minister Philippus Baldaeus described Malabar and Coromandel in 1672.
denomProfiles/reformed-church-in-hungary: Hungary's Calvinist church, centred on Debrecen, the 'Calvinist Rome'.
Confessional basis in the Second Helvetic Confession and the Heidelberg Catechism, adopted at the Synod of Debrecen (1567).
Scripture as the supreme rule of faith and life.
Salvation by grace alone through faith, with a Reformed doctrine of election.
Two sacraments, baptism (including infants) and the Lord's Supper, understood as signs and seals of God's promises.
The Nicene and Apostles' Creeds received as summaries of the catholic faith.
Preserving Hungarian language and identity, especially among minorities in Romania, Slovakia, Ukraine and Serbia.
Church schools and colleges, notably Debrecen (1538) and Sárospatak (1531).
Diaconal and social work through church institutions.
Unity of Hungarian Reformed churches across borders (the Hungarian Reformed Communion, 2009).
Preaching-centred Sunday worship in plain churches, often crowned by a star and a cockerel rather than a cross.
Holy Communion celebrated chiefly at the great feasts (Christmas, Easter, Pentecost) and at harvest.
Metrical psalms from Albert Szenczi Molnár's Hungarian Genevan Psalter (1607).
Confirmation of young people after catechism instruction.
Reading of the Károli Bible (Vizsoly, 1590), the classic Hungarian translation.
Transylvanian Unitarianism
Francis Dávid led part of the Transylvanian Reformed church into anti-Trinitarian teaching in the 1560s.
Hungarian Reformed diaspora
Emigrants founded Hungarian Reformed congregations in North America from the late nineteenth century.
Péter Méliusz Juhász
Bishop of Debrecen who led the 1567 synod and Hungarian Calvinist consolidation.
Gáspár Károli
Pastor of Gönc whose complete Hungarian Bible was printed at Vizsoly in 1590.
Gábor Bethlen
Reformed Prince of Transylvania (1613–29) and patron of Protestant education.
László Tőkés
Reformed pastor in Timișoara whose resistance in December 1989 sparked the Romanian revolution.
About 1.15 million people declared themselves Reformed in Hungary's 2011 census (Hungarian Central Statistical Office); sister churches abroad are not included.
denomProfiles/christian-reformed-church/: Dutch-immigrant Calvinism shaping Christian schools, scholarship and neo-Calvinist thought.
The Three Forms of Unity: Belgic Confession, Heidelberg Catechism and Canons of Dort.
God's sovereignty over every area of life, in the neo-Calvinist tradition of Abraham Kuyper.
Covenant theology, with infant baptism of believers' children.
Contemporary testimony 'Our World Belongs to God' (1986) as a modern statement of faith.
In 2022 its synod declared that the Catechism's condemnation of 'unchastity' includes homosexual sex, giving that view confessional status.
Christian day schools and higher education (Calvin University, Calvin Theological Seminary).
Relief and development through World Renew (founded 1962 as CRWRC).
Broadcast and literature ministry (Back to God Ministries, from 1939).
Integrating faith and learning, including 'Reformed epistemology' in philosophy.
Twice-Sunday worship was long standard, with catechism preaching.
Lord's Supper celebrated several times a year to monthly, after profession of faith.
Psalm and hymn singing from the Psalter Hymnal.
Elders' home visitation and church discipline exercised by the consistory.
Women eligible for all offices since 1995 where a classis permits (local option).
Reformed epistemology
Calvin College philosophers such as Alvin Plantinga and Nicholas Wolterstorff developed it.
Protestant Reformed Churches
Herman Hoeksema's congregations left after the 1924 common-grace controversy.
United Reformed Churches in North America
Conservative congregations left in the 1990s, partly over women in office.
Gijsbert Haan
Leader of the 1857 secession that formed the church.
Louis Berkhof
Calvin Seminary theologian whose Systematic Theology (1932/1938) became widely used.
Alvin Plantinga
Philosopher at Calvin College and Notre Dame, a leading Reformed epistemologist.
Cornelius Van Til
CRC-raised apologist who later taught at Westminster Seminary.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/ta: America's largest Presbyterian church: confessional breadth, social witness, mainline Protestantism.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/co: A Book of Confessions ranging from the Nicene Creed to the Westminster Standards, Barmen, the Confession of 1967 and Belhar.
Jesus Christ as the one Word of God, attested by Scripture.
God's sovereign grace and the 'great ends of the church', including social righteousness.
Ordination of women (elders from 1930, ministers from 1956 in a predecessor church).
Since 2011 no explicit chastity requirement for ordination; marriage redefined as between 'two people' in 2015.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/fo: Social justice advocacy, including peacemaking and anti-racism.
Ecumenical partnerships and mission with churches worldwide.
Theological education through its ten seminaries.
Disaster relief through Presbyterian Disaster Assistance.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/pr: Ordered worship guided by the Book of Common Worship, with sermon at the centre.
Infant baptism and an open table for all baptised Christians.
Government by sessions, presbyteries, synods and a biennial General Assembly.
Ordination of ruling elders and deacons alongside ministers of Word and Sacrament.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/in: Conservatives left its southern predecessor (PCUS) in 1973.
Northern Presbyterian missionaries such as Underwood and Moffett planted it.
American Presbyterian missions in Punjab and north India fed into the 1970 union.
Departures in 1936 and from 2012 formed new Presbyterian bodies.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/ke: Organiser of the first American presbytery (1706).
President of Princeton and the only clergyman to sign the Declaration of Independence.
Princeton theologian of the Old School tradition.
Leading conservative in the fundamentalist–modernist controversy; left in 1936.
Baptist preacher whose 1922 sermon at a Presbyterian pulpit fuelled the controversy.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/me: About 1.14 million members at the end of 2023, according to statistics released by the Office of the General Assembly (2024).
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-usa/in: Its predecessors' missions in Punjab (Ludhiana, from 1834), Allahabad and Kolhapur helped form the United Church of Northern India (1924) and so the Church of North India; partnership links continue.
denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-in-ame: Conservative, confessional Presbyterianism: Westminster Standards, inerrancy and church planting.
The Westminster Confession and Catechisms as its doctrinal standards.
Inerrancy and full authority of Scripture.
Calvinist soteriology: the doctrines of grace and covenant theology.
Ordained offices of elder and deacon reserved for men.
Marriage as between one man and one woman; recent amendments address sexual-identity language for officers.
Church planting in cities and suburbs (Mission to North America; Redeemer City to City).
Campus ministry through Reformed University Fellowship.
World mission through Mission to the World.
Training through Covenant Theological Seminary and Covenant College.
Reverent, preaching-centred worship, ranging from traditional psalm and hymn singing to contemporary styles.
Infant baptism; the Lord's Supper fenced to professing believers.
Elders examine ministers' exceptions to the Westminster Standards ('good faith subscription').
Annual General Assembly with overtures debated by presbyteries.
The Gospel Coalition
Tim Keller co-founded it in 2005 with D. A. Carson.
Redeemer City to City
Keller's network has trained urban church planters internationally.
Evangelism Explosion
D. James Kennedy's evangelism programme (1962) spread worldwide.
D. James Kennedy
Pastor of Coral Ridge Presbyterian and founder of Evangelism Explosion.
Francis Schaeffer
Apologist and founder of L'Abri; joined with the RPCES in 1982.
Tim Keller
Founding pastor of Redeemer Presbyterian, New York (1989).
Ligon Duncan
Theologian and chancellor of Reformed Theological Seminary.
Roughly 390,000 communicant and non-communicant members reported in PCA statistics for 2022.
